# Windows installation engine

The current matching application and setup acceptance uses SSH-signed source `77a570daea41a0bd138a1f2393622ac672cfbe24`. The application contains 4,205 files and 515,617,940 bytes, with manifest SHA-256 `0f7bfda0071d3880e652a989409d8797bf6037997dcc6c4c1d91219c2dee7cc8`. The 517,873,408-byte setup embeds a 36,352-byte launcher and 101,376-byte uninstaller. Its compiler and all 34 recorded source hashes matched before and after acceptance; application and setup source archives were identical. Twenty-four critical runtime files match the isolated build. Portable and repaired installed applications each passed all 32 executable checks; their screenshots were byte-identical and reviewed.

Actual native components loaded the setup image's compiled pins, extracted all 4,212 files, verified the kit, and installed through shipped Node, the unmodified CLI and the production verifier and engine. Both root executables and an actual COM shortcut were placed and journaled under released operation leases. The shortcut used an owned temporary Programs directory; its bytes, single-link status, file identity and directory identity matched the v2 journal.

An owned reader then blocked record removal during a scripted-consent uninstall. All 4,205 release files, the owned shortcut, both root tools and the journal were removed; the installation record was retained and the lease released. The same intact setup kit repaired that installation with the same installation ID, a fresh release, both root tools and a newly journaled shortcut. A repeat returned AlreadyActive and left root tools, shortcut and journals unchanged. After the installed executable checks and an explicit continuation, fresh scripted consent removed the application and exact owned shortcut. Selective cleanup removed all 4,212 extraction files and 656 directories, with none retained. The native harness and driver exited zero. Root, stage and owned boundary were absent afterward; profile, sibling and manual sibling-link markers were unchanged before fixture teardown.

This proves full-payload component composition against an owned temporary installation and Programs directory. Consent was scripted through a hidden native dialog; the production setup and uninstall GUI flows were not driven. Fixed-target GUI/launcher acceptance, actual Start Menu use, registration, final running-helper cleanup, application signing and clean-machine customer acceptance remain open. Verification started no inference or Studio operation.

Directory pins in ownership, operation leases, release removal, stage cleanup and record removal include list-directory access. Attribute-only handles do not enforce delete-sharing restrictions. Three native regressions isolate the actual private pin helpers on empty directories: rename and removal are denied while held and allowed after release. Existing operation and cleanup cases also pass. These pins require list-folder permission and refuse when it is unavailable; identity-only readers keep their existing access.

The installation engine stages verified Windows directory packages and publishes an active release record. A runnable unsigned setup executable composes payload extraction, kit verification, progress and cancellation. Stable launch, shortcuts, uninstall registration and clean-machine acceptance remain delivery gates.

`createWindowsInstallation()` from `scripts/windows-installation.mjs` exposes two host-only operations:

- `install({ bundle, installRoot, signal?, onProgress? })` verifies the complete source package with the production bundle verifier, copies its exact inventory into a fresh release directory, verifies the copy, then publishes `installation.json` through a single file replacement.
- `status(installRoot)` reads bounded installation metadata. Its `integrityVerified: false` explicitly distinguishes a record observation from a verified executable.

A repeated install can recover a recorded release whose entire directory is absent. The engine copies the verified bundle into a fresh exclusive release ID, replaces only that missing record slot and selects the new release. The installation ID, unrelated entries and 32-release limit are preserved; `repairedReleaseId` identifies the replaced slot. Publication rechecks the root, record, releases parent and candidate after the final absence observation. A path that appears is kept, and failed copying leaves the original record. Present partial, changed, redirected or file targets retain their existing refusals, as does a missing releases container. Thirty-nine engine, CLI and boundary cases cover the repair and unchanged contracts, including a deterministic moved-parent regression. Native component composition also covers a journal-blocked partial uninstall followed by same-bundle recovery and a fresh consented uninstall. The matching full-payload acceptance above exercises this repair after a record-blocked uninstall; the journal-blocked component case remains separate evidence.

The installer host chooses the program directory. The engine requires its parent to exist and admits only an empty new directory or a valid existing Arcane installation. App profiles and projects remain separate. Updates retain previous releases and unrelated files. Failed candidates remain available for inspection and are never automatically adopted or removed.

On Windows, admission reserves the complete release and bundled runtime path below 260 characters. This check happens before verification or target mutation: copying files successfully alone cannot establish that Windows can start a child from that directory. See Microsoft's [current-directory restriction](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-setcurrentdirectory). No machine path policy is changed.

An exclusive operation lock fences concurrent installers. Its identity and contents are checked throughout the operation. Changed records, locks, copied files, directories, extra entries, links and junctions refuse publication. The final tree must match the verified inventory, including when reactivating a retained release. Filesystem checks use cooperative ownership and identity; operating-system isolation remains separate.

An optional `AbortSignal` cancels before publication, retaining the previous selection and the candidate. Cancellation after completed publication still reports the installed release. The trusted, synchronous `onProgress` observer returns `undefined` and receives frozen phase/file/byte counters. It supplies presentation metadata rather than installation authority.

Failures preserve the primary cause and report `published: false`, `true` or `null` for retained selection, completed publication or unconfirmed publication. Lock-cleanup failures are retained separately. There is no automatic retry, stale-lock takeover, program launch, shortcut creation, registry write or profile deletion. Retention is bounded to 32 recorded releases; removal and interrupted-install recovery need their own explicit host workflow.

Focused tests use actual temporary filesystems with a labelled small-inventory verifier. Full package acceptance uses the production verifier and separately records the engine source hash and bundle manifest. Neither fixture coverage nor package copying establishes a complete installer or an authenticated customer task.

`createWindowsSetupPayload()` from `scripts/windows-setup-payload.mjs` streams a deterministic stored ZIP containing the verified bundle and a fixed five-module installation kit. The kit manifest independently pins the bundle manifest, bundled Node and each kit file; the returned receipt also pins the entire payload and kit manifest. Changed inputs or replaced outputs refuse acceptance and retain the candidate. The actual C# reader extracts the writer's data-descriptor format in a separate console fixture.

`KitVerifier.Verify(stage, expectedKitManifestSha256)` supplies the separate check before executing extracted code. It admits exactly the fixed installation modules, checks their hashes and sizes, checks the bundled Node hash and x64 PE header, and binds the bundle manifest to its approved hash. Unexpected kit entries and redirected ancestors refuse admission. Native C# harness tests use synthetic runtimes without executing them. These filesystem checks assume cooperative ownership; they do not isolate the installer from other processes running as the same user.

The signed installation-engine snapshot `b898ff2c9749e13a285f9228370bed74acd7917e` installed the existing application package from `186787684c1b964ea03c02d10c00c474889dcb5a` into a fresh owned temporary directory. Production verification covered all 4,174 payload files and the manifest before and after copying; activation took 67,955 ms and retained the separate profile fixture. The installed executable then passed all 32 startup, renderer, bundled MCP and shutdown checks in 32,555 ms. Its screenshot was reviewed. The application manifest remains `d4f015fd7275886ced9f784c6ce4efffc2d812efaec54eb8fe985ac810e422ae`; later application changes are excluded. No setup GUI, shortcuts, registration, application signature, provider inference or Studio operation was involved.

## Setup executable

On Windows x64, build setup from an existing verified bundle and an existing output directory:

```powershell
npm run package:setup -- --bundle "C:\ArcaneBuild\Bundle" --output-parent "C:\ArcaneBuild\Output"
```

The build uses the in-box .NET Framework compiler and emits a unique directory containing `Arcane-Setup.exe`, its payload and a build receipt. The receipt pins native sources, build helpers, icon, compiler and kit files. Payload and kit-manifest hashes are compiled into the executable; assembly rechecks every copied input. The build never launches setup. Setup runs as the current user and selects `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Arcane` after the human clicks Install. Bundled Node supplies installation execution; the installed customer needs no separate Node or npm installation. Native components require .NET Framework 4.7.2 or later; clean-machine runtime acceptance remains open.

The [internal protocol](WINDOWS_INSTALLER_PROTOCOL.md) carries bounded progress and exactly one terminal result. Closing during work requests cancellation and waits for the actual outcome. The UI distinguishes unchanged selection, completed publication and unconfirmed state. It neither retries automatically nor kills active installation work.

Temporary-stage selection expands existing short path aliases and reserves the complete payload path budget. Successful extraction records each created file's bytes, hash and handle identity, and each directory's identity. After a confirmed outcome, cleanup consumes that receipt once and deletes only unchanged owned files through verified handles and owned empty directories. Added, edited, replaced, hardlinked or redirected entries remain. Unconfirmed work, extraction/kit failures and cleanup failures retain their files and report retention without changing the installation result.

The integrated native components were compiled with the actual setup sources and exercised through a separate acceptance harness against the real appended payload. They installed the existing application bundle through its extracted, verified Node and CLI, acknowledged the selected release, then removed all 4,181 extracted files and 655 directories. The active record matched the result, the stage was absent afterward, and the separate profile fixture was unchanged. All 16 build-source hashes matched the executable's receipt. Idle native controls were rendered and reviewed without input. This proves component composition with an owned temporary target; the production GUI was not clicked, the fixed user Programs target was not used, and neither registration nor shortcuts were created. This candidate still contains application source `186787684c1b964ea03c02d10c00c474889dcb5a`; integration of a newer application rebuild, signed distribution and complete customer acceptance remain separate gates.

## Stable launcher component

`InstalledLauncher` reads the strict active-release record, checks the selected manifest and verifies the size, hash and x64 PE identity of the executable it starts. It keeps deny-write handles through one direct launch, rechecks the root and current selection, forwards no arguments and never falls back to an older release. `FullBundleVerified` remains false: other bundle files are not rehashed per launch. The production entry derives its root from its own executable directory and accepts no alternate-root flags.

Native fixtures compile and run the actual launcher against owned console peers, covering retained-release selection, tampering, malformed metadata, redirects, locks and selection changes. The same fixtures pass with an existing short-name TEMP alias after native canonicalization. Shortcuts, registration and launching the real installed application retain their integration and customer-acceptance gates.

`OwnedFiles` supplies the separate placement primitive. It publishes approved bytes without overwriting a path, and replaces or removes an existing file only when its descriptor still matches the root identity, file identity, length and hash. Changed, unrecorded, linked or redirected files stay in place. An interrupted replacement reports its retained previous bytes; a mapped previous executable may also remain in a reported backup. Native fixtures cover these outcomes with explicit peer readiness and terminal acknowledgement. Root pinning and checks retain cooperative limits against ancestor changes by the same user. Postinstall orchestration remains separate.

`SetupOwnership` records those descriptors in a bounded, strict journal bound to the engine installation ID and root identity. Foreign, malformed, linked or redirected journals are kept. Every save, including an identical save, checks the currently observed journal identity and bytes through ownership-aware placement and fences the installation record before and after. Saved descriptors record past placement; they do not prove that a file remains intact. Native fixtures cover round trips, concurrent edits, changed selections and interrupted publication. Postinstall integration, shortcuts and registration retain their own gates.

`ArcaneShellLink` creates and reads bounded shortcut bytes through in-memory Windows COM streams. The fixed fields select the canonical launcher, installation working directory and icon, with empty arguments. Inspection reports fields without resolving or starting a target; matching fields grant no target ownership or integrity. Native fixtures cover actual serialization, malformed bytes and unsafe target paths. The placement workflow is described below.

`PostInstall.CompleteShortcut` connects that link builder to setup. After root-tool completion it independently verifies both recorded files, acquires the matching operation lease and places only `Arcane.lnk` in the current user Programs directory supplied by the trusted host. It creates no directory and preserves manual or changed links. The bounded v2 ownership journal records the external directory and file identities; v1 journals remain supported, and existing root-tool saves preserve the shortcut. Repeated setup reuses verified link bytes; a missing owned link can be recreated. Consented uninstall independently matches the current Programs directory and its identity before removing the exact owned link, after recorded releases and before root tools. A changed link or destination is kept and reported while removal of the recorded application continues. An earlier cancellation or release refusal retains the shortcut. Fifty-nine focused native cases pass across the journal, root tools, shortcut completion, consented removal, setup form, installed handoff, customer messages and registration plan; 23 packaging cases pass with the updated source closure. These tests use owned temporary Programs fixtures and scripted consent. The matching `77a570d` full-payload composition above includes this integration; actual Start Menu use and fixed-target GUI acceptance remain separate gates.

`InstallationActivity` provides a separate read-only Restart Manager snapshot for up to three caller-owned canonical files. A single count-only query reports Idle, Busy or Unknown without fetching process identities or terminating anything. Owned native peers cover running images, held ordinary files and acknowledged exits. Idle proves neither ownership nor safe removal; the future uninstall workflow must preserve its own identity and operation fences. Other sessions, elevated applications, services and DLL loads remain unverified.

`RegistrationPlanner` prepares nine fixed current-user uninstall values from a matching record, ownership journal and verified placement descriptors. It emits literal strings and DWORD values, including a quoted direct uninstall path with no flags. It performs no registry or filesystem access.

`PostInstall.CompleteRegistration` connects that plan to setup after both approved root tools are confirmed. Under the installation operation lease it saves a v4 pending intent before calling the registry store. The intent binds a random owner to the exact typed-value hash; the previous confirmed descriptor remains separate. The store writes the ten values, including its owner marker, in one native transaction. Confirmed completion records the descriptor and clears the intent, returning to the canonical v3 journal. Existing root-file and shortcut saves preserve pending work, and v1-v3 journal bytes remain compatible.

Recovery admits only the previous exact descriptor, the exact pending owner and typed-value hash for the installation, or observed absence. A matching owner alone grants no authority. Setup reconciles pending work before preparing the current release's plan, including when the installation engine has upgraded the release. Removal resolves the same authority and deletes through a transacted handle after fresh consent. Edited entries are kept and reported; interrupted transactions, native query failures and unconfirmed registry targets retain the journal and root tools for review or a later consented attempt. An unconfirmed operation lease still requires review and is never taken over automatically.

Native component fixtures cover atomic creation and update, rollback with the prior last-write time preserved, commit before acknowledgement, exact-intent recovery, forged intents, changed values and subkeys, interrupted deletion and fresh-consent removal. Lifecycle fixtures also cover durable intent publication, record and journal changes, and recovery followed by an actual fixture-engine upgrade. Registry checks use exclusively created volatile current-user fixture parents and never open the production uninstall namespace. These results do not prove fixed-target registration, Apps & Features behavior, production GUI interaction, application signing or clean-machine acceptance; the full-payload snapshot above predates this integration.

`OperationLease` exclusively creates and holds `installation.lock`, binding its exact bytes and file identity to an authorized root and record. Ordinary readers, the engine and launcher remain excluded. Explicit lease-aware reads accept only that live issued capability. Release deletes its unchanged lock through the held handle once; disposal or a crashed holder retains the lock without takeover. Native fixtures cover engine exclusion, blocked tampering, changed records, release and stale-lock retention. This supplies operation fencing for future removal; no uninstall workflow is implied.

The ownership journal also supplies explicit lease-aware read and save overloads. They require the matching live capability, preserve the observed journal's compare-and-swap and fence record identity before and after publication. Ordinary access remains excluded by a lock. Native fixtures cover null, foreign, released and disposed capabilities, both manual-file race timings and changed record identities without claiming an unconfirmed save.

`ReleaseRemoval` removes only a release selected from the leased record and its pinned manifest. It admits the exact executable entry before deletion, checks known activity, removes that launch target first, and verifies listed bytes through the same handles that delete them. Directory pins and path identities prevent adoption of newly appearing directories; only unchanged empty directories are removed. Manual content retains the manifest for later explicit cleanup. Private native path handling supports long descendants already admitted by the installation engine without widening root inputs. Ten native cases cover completion, busy peers, tampering, partial counts, interrupted work and long file/directory paths. Manifest entries authorize matching bytes rather than historical file identities, and filesystem guarantees remain cooperative.

`UninstallConsent` displays the exact version and literal path in selectable fields, defaults to Cancel and constructs an in-memory authorization only through the Uninstall handler. That authorization is consumed once against the matching live lease, record and journal; changed state requires a new decision. Five owned scripted-modal cases cover control wiring, refusal before a dialog opens, record/journal changes, replay and the complete 64-character version fitting its native field. The actual controls were rendered and reviewed. These checks establish component behaviour, separate from physical keyboard, accessibility, DPI and customer acceptance.

`UninstallTransaction` binds that displayed decision to one installation operation. It checks activity across every recorded application and bundled Node executable plus the owned root executables, in batches of three. It removes retained releases before the active release, then the journal-owned files, journal and installation record last. Fresh record and journal checks guard each phase; partial work keeps its measured results, and every handled terminal path attempts release of its exact operation lease. Empty containers are removed only through handles with the original directory identity. Manual files, profiles and siblings remain. A changed container is reported separately from ordinary retained content. Ten native cases cover these behaviours, including 32 recorded releases, cancellation, interrupted work and a replaced nonempty container. The tests use engine-created temporary installations and scripted consent. Self-uninstaller handoff and setup delivery remain integration work; this component is not yet exposed by the installed application.

`UninstallForm` runs the consent-bound transaction on a worker and keeps the window responsive. Closing during work requests cancellation; the window remains open until the worker returns its actual result. Terminal messages distinguish completion, refusal, partial work and retained operation records. Late progress cannot replace those messages. Three hidden native-window cases cover completion, missing authorization and closing during acknowledged work, using temporary installations and scripted consent. Physical input, DPI, accessibility and the installed entrypoint remain acceptance gates.

`UninstallStage` prepares a verified copy of the journal-owned uninstaller in an exclusively created temporary container. Creation and opening use one native call relative to a pinned parent. Directory pins include list access so their sharing rules actually block renames. The issued handoff pin checks the source again and holds the verified copy and its container against writes and removal. Cleanup attempts only the unchanged issued file and empty original container once, retaining manual content and completed deletion evidence. Eight native cases cover staging, source and copy changes, pin enforcement, failed preparation and selective cleanup. This component never executes the copy or grants uninstall permission.

`UninstallEntry` starts that verified copy with an inherited, restricted wait handle for the original process. The staged image waits for actual termination, then rechecks its image, the installed source and ownership journal before showing fresh consent. Command-line arguments never skip the decision. Invalid numeric handles are duplicated privately for validation; they cannot close unrelated handles. Seven native cases cover exit ordering, timeout, malformed input, handle safety and the complete entrypoint path with scripted Confirm or Cancel on owned installations. An invalid parent identity is refused before consent. The confirmed case removes the recorded installation; Cancel keeps it unchanged. The temporary running copy remains explicitly retained. These checks do not establish fixed-target setup delivery, physical input, clean-machine behaviour or application signing.

Setup progress is also bound to its original installation operation. Late reports are discarded when that operation ends, including while Open Arcane reuses the busy state. A hidden native-control regression posts from an acknowledged background thread and dispatches real UI messages. The original callback raised exceptions in both stale-operation cases; the same four cases pass with the identity guard. This proves callback handling, separate from GUI customer acceptance.

The setup builder compiles and embeds separate stable launcher and uninstaller executables, each with its own size and SHA-256 pin. After a confirmed engine outcome, `PostInstall.CompleteRootFiles` checks the matching installation and selected release, validates both sources, and acquires an operation lease. It places and records the launcher before touching the uninstaller, preserving completed ownership if a later step fails. It then places and records the uninstaller and confirms the final journal. Readiness requires both exact descriptors and release of the lease. Six native pair-completion cases cover approved and manual files, source pins, changed state, replacements and partial evidence; eight existing launcher cases remain passing. Open Arcane requires pair readiness and separately re-verifies the selected executable. The fixed-target GUI, actual setup delivery and customer acceptance remain separate gates.

All 32 actual executable checks passed, 24 critical files matched the isolated build and the workspace screenshot was reviewed. The runnable setup is 517,474,719 bytes; all 23 build-source hashes matched its receipt. Actual native components extracted that payload, installed through its verified bundled runtime, placed and journaled the 31,232-byte embedded launcher, then selectively removed all 4,201 stage files and 656 directories. The stage was absent and the profile fixture unchanged. Both portable and installed application passed all 32 executable checks; 24 critical files matched the isolated build and the screenshots were identical and reviewed. This used a separate harness and owned temporary target. The fixed-target GUI, Start Menu placement, registration, uninstall, application signing, clean-machine and complete customer acceptance remain open.
